about: Approved mileage rates and how mileage allowance and relief work, for tools/build-mileage-pages.js, quoted from GOV.UK. Rates in pence per business mile.

rates.quote: Approved mileage rates — Vehicle / Flat rate per business mile for the 2026 to 2027 tax year / Flat rate per business mile before 6 April 2026: Cars and goods vehicles first 10,000 miles 55p 45p; Cars and goods vehicles after 10,000 miles 25p 25p; Motorcycles 24p 24p; Bicycles 20p 20p

example.quote: Your employee travels 12,000 business miles in their car - the approved amount for the year would be £6,000 (10,000 × 55p plus 2,000 × 25p).

excess.quote: Anything above the ‘approved amount’: You must either: report on form P11D; add anything above the ‘approved amount’ to the employee’s pay, and deduct and pay tax as normal

ni.quote: National Insurance: rates per business mile — Cars and vans 55p from 6 April 2026 (45p before 6 April 2026); Motorcycles 24p; Bikes 20p … add the excess to their other earnings for that earnings period when calculating Class 1 National Insurance (but not Pay As You Earn (PAYE) tax)

covers.quote: This covers the cost of owning and running your vehicle. You cannot claim separately for things like: fuel, electricity, vehicle tax, MOTs, repairs

shortfall.quote: take away any amount your employer pays you towards your costs, (sometimes called a ‘mileage allowance’)

commute.quote: This does not include travelling to and from your work, unless it’s a temporary place of work.

years.quote: You can claim for the current tax year and the 4 previous tax years, if you’re eligible.

reliefRate.quote: You’ll get tax relief based on what you’ve spent and the rate at which you pay tax. Example: If you claim £60 and pay tax at a rate of 20% in that year, the amount you are entitled to is £12 (20% of £60).

passenger.quote: If your employee carries another employee in their own car or van on a business journey, you can pay them passenger payments of up to 5p per mile tax-free.

logs.quote: When you claim, you must send HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) copies of your mileage logs.
